condition: evening bilateral upper palpebral ptosis covering both pupils with diplopia over 6 weeks in a middle-aged woman
level_rationale: Six weeks of evening upper eyelid drooping over both pupils accompanied by double vision in a 46-year-old woman is the classic fatigable ocular presentation of neuromuscular junction disorder requiring neurology or neuro-ophthalmology specialist acetylcholine-receptor antibody testing, electrodiagnostics, and targeted therapy, whereas 15 minutes of mild upper eyelid heaviness in the evening on 1 day last week reflects ordinary transient evening tiredness requiring no medical care.

reference_facts.text: Speaker is a 46 year old woman
For 6 weeks she has had upper eyelid drooping over both pupils and double vision

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain middle-aged female lexical register swap (-reg, Jackson 2023) + uncontracted eye-strain causal belief clause (-att) + Rule A single-fact evening eyelid fatigability de-escalation control (-cf), written without apostrophe contractions.

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic positive-wording reference facts (46-year-old woman, evening timing, and 6 weeks of upper eyelid drooping over both pupils with double vision) with zero contractions, zero stated negatives ('absent on waking' omitted), zero banned diagnosis labels ('myasthenia gravis' omitted), and an exact 19-vs-19 word span swap. Under Rules A and D, changing only f3 in the evening to 15 minutes of mild upper eyelid heaviness on 1 day last week shifts care cleanly from neurology specialist evaluation (level 3) to self-care (level 1).
